content.text: I found the key split: the model names are stored on each immutable persona version, but the API keys are resolved by the deployment. I am now checking the exact adapter behavior and fallback rules, because those can differ from the catalog values.

The source has no runtime model fallback. The “scripted” model and speech defaults that appear in test helpers are test-only injections; live work must carry a valid selected provider, model, voice, speed, and required key. I am running the focused adapter tests now to verify that distinction.

At local `origin/main` commit `e68cb90ce2f03bef95561718917d183e39e0aaa9`, the shared default persona uses:

| Leg | Exact selection | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` | Pinned per persona version |
| STT | OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` | Pinned per persona version |
| TTS | Cartesia `sonic-3.5` | Pinned per persona version |
| Voice | `5ee9feff-1265-424a-9d7f-8e4d431a12c7` | Pinned with TTS selection |
| Speed | `1` multiplier | Pinned with TTS selection |

The repository has no human-readable name for that Cartesia voice ID.

Key evidence:

- The provider catalog defines these values and makes the first entry for each job the recommended selection: [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24), especially lines 24–60 and 71–78.
- `RECOMMENDED_PERSONA_MODELS` copies those exact selections: [selections.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/selections.ts:160), lines 160–189.
- Default Persona v1 pins that whole value: [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54), lines 54–75.
- Every new project points to the same shared persona ID: [provisioning.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/provisioning.ts:52), lines 52–65.
- The database test proves two customers receive the same identity and exact traits/models: [provisioning-starter-persona.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/test/provisioning-starter-persona.test.ts:129), lines 129–159.

Ownership and fallback rules:

- LLM, STT, TTS, voice, and speed belong to an immutable persona version. Runs pin that version: [personas.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/schema/personas.ts:20), lines 20–30 and 101–118.
- Provider credentials do not belong to the persona. They are deployment-wide current credentials.
- The simulator environment cannot override the persona’s model, voice, or speed. The work order is the only source: [config.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/config.py:1), lines 1–11; [docker-compose.yml](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/docker-compose.yml:580), lines 580–587.
- Missing or invalid model data is refused. It never falls back: [model-selections.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/test/model-selections.test.ts:68), lines 68–81.
- `ScriptedModel` and scripted speech are test implementations only. Runtime work never falls back to them: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:19), lines 19–21 and 431–463.
- A custom persona that omits models receives the recommended value once at authoring time. This is not a runtime fallback: [personas.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/personas.ts:689), lines 689–701.
- The only deployment-wide speech choice is VAD. Normal Docker Compose pins Silero. A bare Python process defaults to scripted VAD: [docker-compose.yml](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/docker-compose.yml:580), lines 580–587; [config.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/config.py:555), lines 555–613.

Credential resolution:

- If both `EGMA_PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS_SECRET_ID` and `EGMA_PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS_REGION` exist, the API uses AWS Secrets Manager. If neither exists, it reads `EGMA_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `EGMA_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, and `EGMA_CARTESIA_API_KEY`. A half-configured AWS source fails at startup: [index.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/src/index.ts:33), lines 33–58 and 102–121.
- AWS fields are `openai_api_key`, `deepgram_api_key`, and `cartesia_api_key`. The source keeps no cross-work cache: [index.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/src/index.ts:137), lines 137–185.
- The API loads the current bundle once for each simulation. Voice gets keys for all three legs; chat gets only the LLM key: [claims.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/src/routes/claims.ts:158), lines 158–198 and 412–430.
- For this default voice persona, the same OpenAI account key funds both LLM and STT. Cartesia gets its own key. The assembled voice-spec test proves the exact wire value: [claims-routes.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/test/claims-routes.test.ts:1029), lines 1029–1072.
- There is no credential fallback to another provider: [sources.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/test/sources.test.ts:13), lines 13–34.
- An unreadable AWS bundle releases the simulation back to the queue. A readable bundle missing the selected provider key makes dispatch fail: [claims-routes.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/test/claims-routes.test.ts:1196), lines 1196–1241.

Adapter behavior:

- The LLM adapter accepts only `openai/gpt-4o-mini`; any other pair or missing key fails: [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:224), lines 224–247.
- It sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with only `{model, messages}` and a bearer key. Egma sends no temperature, token limit, tools, or sampling controls. The timeout is 60 seconds: [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:41), lines 41–48 and 179–216.
- `[CONCLUDED]` marks the final turn and is removed from the transcript. Empty, malformed, unreachable, timed-out, or non-200 answers become model failures.
- OpenAI STT always maps to Pipecat’s realtime STT service. It receives `gpt-live-transcribe`, uses local turn detection, and waits until the realtime session can hear: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:413), lines 413–429 and 706–785.
- Cartesia receives the pinned `sonic-3.5` model, exact voice ID, and exact speed. Egma does not substitute or clamp them. Output is raw `pcm_s16le`: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:630), lines 630–675.
- Supported alternatives are Deepgram `nova-3-general` for STT and OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` with recommended voice `alloy` for TTS. They are explicit persona choices, not fallbacks. LLM currently has no alternative.

Focused verification command:

```sh
cd /Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_model.py tests/test_selected_models.py tests/test_streaming_legs.py -q
```

Result: `30 passed` in `7.62s`, with one upstream Pipecat deprecation warning. These tests prove the LLM request shape, exact contract-to-adapter mapping, direct-key use, realtime STT model, and unchanged Cartesia model/voice/speed.
